mainEntity.name: What is the New York Dispensary Visibility Index?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a database measuring how New York cannabis dispensaries appear in ChatGPT recommendations across a standardized set of local discovery prompts. Each published dispensary gets a public profile with its score, prompt-by-prompt results and the competitors ChatGPT surfaced.

mainEntity.name: What is ChatGPT Visibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: ChatGPT Visibility measures whether a dispensary appears in ChatGPT recommendations and where it is positioned within the answer. It is scored 0–100 by weighting three market-level averages: 70% primary market, 20% secondary market and 10% regional market.

mainEntity.name: Why isn't my dispensary showing up in ChatGPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually it is not a judgment about the business. AI systems leave out businesses they cannot verify confidently. Inconsistent name, address and phone data across directories, thin or unclaimed listings, low review response rates and no third-party editorial coverage are the common causes. A dispensary can rank well on Google and still fail that confidence threshold.

mainEntity.name: Where does ChatGPT get local business information from?

acceptedAnswer.text: ChatGPT Search can combine information from the open web and third-party data providers when generating local recommendations. The exact source mix can vary by query, location and product experience, which is one reason we measure the resulting recommendation itself rather than assuming visibility from any single directory.

mainEntity.name: Does a good Google ranking mean good ChatGPT visibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. In SOCi's 2026 Local Visibility Index, only 45% of retail brands leading Google's local results also appeared in AI recommendations. The two run on different inputs and should be measured separately.

mainEntity.name: How many prompts are tested?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ten standardized recommendation prompts per dispensary: six in the Primary Market, two in the Secondary Market and two in the Regional Market. Each prompt is run and the resulting ChatGPT response is recorded, so every result reflects an actual recommendation appearance rather than an inferred one.

mainEntity.name: What does "Not mentioned" mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dispensary did not appear in the ChatGPT response recorded for that specific prompt on the check date. It scores zero points for that prompt.

mainEntity.name: Why is my profile marked Pending?

acceptedAnswer.text: A public composite score is published only once all 10 standardized prompts return a valid result. If a request fails, times out, or cannot be validated, the profile stays Pending until the missing check completes successfully — we do not publish a score from a partial scan.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from Weedmaps or Leafly rankings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Weedmaps and Leafly rank dispensaries inside their own platforms, using their own listings and reviews. The Index does not rank anything itself. It records what ChatGPT says when asked a neutral question, and reports the result.

mainEntity.name: Is Gemini included?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The current public benchmark covers ChatGPT only. Other AI providers may be published as separate datasets once their data is reliable enough to report.

mainEntity.name: Are Google rankings included?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not in the public score. Google Organic and Google Maps analysis is available through the Full Visibility Report.

mainEntity.name: Is Menu SEO included in the public score?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Menu SEO can be analyzed as part of the Full Visibility Report but is not part of the public composite score.

mainEntity.name: How often are results updated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Profiles are rechecked periodically because AI recommendations change. Every profile shows the date of its most recent check.

mainEntity.name: My score looks wrong. Can I get it rechecked?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Request a recheck through the Full Visibility Report form and we will re-run the standardized prompt set and update the profile with a new check date.

mainEntity.name: Who runs the New York Dispensary Visibility Index?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tarasovs Digital Agency, a remote-first agency serving New York and US clients. The agency also sells dispensary SEO services, which is disclosed on this page. Every dispensary is measured with the same prompt set and the same scoring, and profiles are published whether the score is high or low.

mainEntity.name: How is the ChatGPT Visibility score calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Recorded results receive 100 points for #1, 85 for #2, 70 for #3, 55 for #4–5, 40 for an unranked mention and 0 for no mention. Market scores are combined using 70% Primary, 20% Secondary and 10% Regional weighting.

mainEntity.name: Why can a dispensary's score change?

acceptedAnswer.text: A public score is published only after all 10 standardized checks have a documented result. A partial benchmark remains Pending and is excluded from the statistics and ranking.

title: Dutchie Menu SEO for Dispensaries

seo.description: Make your Dutchie menu, categories, and product pages crawlable, indexable, and connected to your site's SEO — so your inventory ranks and drives orders.

mainEntity.name: Can Google actually index my Dutchie menu?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your configuration. The default embedded iFrame is only partially indexed, while Dutchie Pro (root-domain) and Dutchie+ serve fully crawlable product pages. We audit what's indexed today and fix how your menu is served so pages can be crawled.

mainEntity.name: Why aren't my Dutchie products showing up in search?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually because the menu is embedded in a cross-origin iFrame Google doesn't crawl as part of your page, there's no Product schema on your domain, and product pages are thin or duplicated. Those are exactly the issues a menu SEO engagement fixes.

mainEntity.name: What's the best Dutchie setup for SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most dispensaries, Dutchie Pro (or Pro + Proxy) is best because your menu is served on your root domain with real product URLs and schema. We generally avoid a subdomain-only menu, since Google treats subdomains as separate sites.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Dutchie Pro to do menu SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can win some ground on an embedded menu, but the ceiling is low. Real product-level ranking needs indexable pages on your domain — which is why we often pair menu SEO with a move to Dutchie Pro.

mainEntity.name: Will a subdomain menu hurt my SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's better than a fully hidden iFrame, but Google treats a subdomain as a separate site, so authority, local relevance, and internal links don't fully flow to your main domain. Root-domain configurations consolidate that value instead.

mainEntity.name: Can you optimize product pages for specific strains and products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We give categories and high-value products unique, compliant descriptions, add product schema, and build category hubs — while fixing duplication so similar products don't compete with each other.

mainEntity.name: How does menu SEO help with AI search?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI assistants recommend and cite from clear, crawlable, structured pages. Indexable product pages with schema are what make your inventory eligible to be the answer when someone asks an assistant for a product near them.

title: Dutchie Pro Migration SEO | Migrate Without Losing Rankings

mainEntity.name: When is Dutchie Plus being sunset?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dutchie has said it will support legacy Dutchie Plus customers through the end of 2026. Exact end-of-life dates are tier-dependent, so request a written timeline from your Dutchie account manager and plan to complete migration well before the API stops responding.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Dutchie iFrame and Dutchie Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: The default iFrame embeds your menu from Dutchie's domain inside a frame, which search engines struggle to index as real pages. Dutchie Pro serves store and product pages as standalone, crawlable URLs on your own domain, so each can be found, ranked, and cited individually.

mainEntity.name: Will migrating to Dutchie Pro hurt my SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if it's done without proper URL mapping and redirects. The real risks are URL changes without 301s, dropped metadata, broken internal links, and stale schema. We map every indexed URL before migration and preserve structure wherever possible — which is why Verdi's rankings grew through the migration instead of dropping.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Dutchie Pro migration take to show results?

acceptedAnswer.text: Indexing of newly crawlable pages typically begins within the first few weeks. Meaningful ranking and traffic gains build over 3–6 months as Google gains confidence in the new URLs — consistent with the six-month window behind the Verdi results.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to leave Dutchie to fix my menu SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If you're happy with Dutchie operationally, migrating to Dutchie Pro keeps your POS, staff, and customer accounts while making your menu indexable. Switching providers only makes sense if you were already planning to leave for other reasons.

mainEntity.name: Can you migrate a multi-location / MSO setup?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Multi-location migrations need more URL mapping and per-location QA, and we scope the timeline accordingly. Store-location pages are usually among the biggest winners, since each becomes an indexable, locally relevant page instead of a menu tab.

mainEntity.name: What does a Dutchie Pro migration cost?

mainEntity.name: What is GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)?

acceptedAnswer.text: GEO — Generative Engine Optimization — is the discipline of optimizing website content, structured data, and brand authority signals so that AI-powered search engines — including ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot — cite your brand in their generated responses. Unlike traditional SEO, which targets search engine rankings, GEO targets the AI layer that now answers a growing share of user queries directly, without requiring a website click.

mainEntity.name: How is GEO different from SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional SEO optimizes for keyword rankings in Google's blue-link results. GEO optimizes for citations in AI-generated answers. The two disciplines share some foundations — quality content, technical site health, authority signals — but GEO requires additional practices: structured content architecture for AI retrieval, FAQPage schema, prompt-aligned content, E-E-A-T authority building, and Share of Model measurement. In 2026, businesses need both.

mainEntity.name: How long does GEO take to show results?

acceptedAnswer.text: First AI citations typically appear within 4–8 weeks for well-optimized content in low-to-medium competition topics. New content enters AI citation pools within 3–5 business days on most platforms, though competitive queries take longer to penetrate. Share of Model improvements become measurable within the first 60 days. Sustained authority in competitive niches typically takes 3–6 months, similar to traditional SEO timelines.

mainEntity.name: How do you measure GEO results?

acceptedAnswer.text: We measure GEO through Share of Model (SoM) — the percentage of relevant AI queries where your brand is cited. Each month, we test a predefined set of 50–100 queries across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Copilot, and document where your brand appears, in what position, and with what context. We also track citation growth on Clutch, industry publications, and other third-party sources that feed AI model training.

mainEntity.name: Can GEO work alongside my existing SEO strategy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — and it works better when it does. GEO and traditional SEO share the same technical foundation: fast-loading, crawlable sites with strong content and authority signals. The GEO-specific additions — structured content, FAQ schema, E-E-A-T optimization — also improve traditional SEO performance. Tarasovs manages both disciplines in an integrated strategy so they reinforce rather than duplicate each other.

mainEntity.name: What is GEO and why is it included in your web design projects?

mainEntity.name: What is Share of Model and how do you track it?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common reasons are: AI crawlers are blocked by your robots.txt or CDN configuration; your content lacks the structured Q&A format that AI retrieval systems prefer; your site has low E-E-A-T signals and is not recognized as an authoritative source; your brand is not mentioned on independent third-party domains that AI models use for corroboration; or your content is rendered client-side in JavaScript, which many AI bots cannot process. mainEntity.name: What is responsive web design?

acceptedAnswer.text: Responsive web design is an approach that allows a website to automatically adapt its layout, content, navigation, and functionality to different screen sizes and devices, including desktops, tablets, and smartphones.

mainEntity.name: Why does my business need a responsive website?

acceptedAnswer.text: A responsive website gives visitors a consistent and accessible experience across devices. It makes content easier to read, improves navigation, supports user engagement, and helps reduce friction that may prevent visitors from taking action.

mainEntity.name: Do you use a mobile-first design approach?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We begin with the mobile experience so essential content, functionality, and user journeys are prioritized from the start. The design is then expanded and optimized for tablets, laptops, and desktop screens.

mainEntity.name: Will the website work on different screen sizes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We create flexible layouts that adjust to a wide range of screen sizes and resolutions, helping the website remain functional, readable, and visually consistent across current devices.

mainEntity.name: How do you optimize navigation for mobile devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: We design clear navigation structures, mobile-friendly menus, readable layouts, and controls optimized for touch interactions. This helps visitors find important information and move through the website without unnecessary difficulty.

mainEntity.name: Will a responsive website load quickly on mobile networks?

acceptedAnswer.text: We optimize responsive websites for speed and performance across devices and connection types. This can include efficient layouts, optimized media, clean development, and careful loading of website resources.

mainEntity.name: Can you make my existing website responsive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We can review an existing website, identify problems across mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts, and determine whether it should be improved, rebuilt, or redesigned to provide a consistent responsive experience.

mainEntity.name: How do you test a responsive website?

acceptedAnswer.text: We test layouts, navigation, content readability, touch interactions, and functionality across multiple viewport sizes and modern browsers to identify issues before the website is launched.

mainEntity.name: What services does Tarasovs Digital Agency offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tarasovs Digital Agency offers web design, Framer and Webflow development, WordPress development, SEO, GEO (AI search optimization), UI/UX design, e-commerce, digital marketing, content management, and analytics. Every service is built around one outcome: your business performing better online — in Google, in AI search, and with the clients that matter.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with businesses outside New York?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Tarasovs is a remote-first agency serving clients across the United States, United Kingdom, and Europe. All project work is managed remotely with no compromise on quality or responsiveness.

mainEntity.name: Can you handle both web design and SEO in one project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Tarasovs integrates web design, development, and SEO from the start. Every site ships with technical SEO foundations, schema markup, Core Web Vitals optimization, and GEO-ready content structure included by default.

mainEntity.name: What is GEO and why does it matter in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: GEO — Generative Engine Optimization — is the practice of structuring website content so that AI-powered platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews cite your brand in their generated responses. In 2026, AI search is one of the fastest-growing discovery channels. Businesses that appear in AI answers receive high-intent referrals at no cost per click.

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical web design project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most business websites take 6–10 weeks from kickoff to launch. Framer projects typically take 3–5 weeks. E-commerce builds take 8–14 weeks depending on scope.

mainEntity.name: Which platform do you build websites on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tarasovs builds on Framer, Webflow, and WordPress — recommending the platform based on project needs. Framer is best for design-heavy marketing sites. Webflow suits content-heavy sites with complex CMS needs. WordPress is best for large-scale sites and e-commerce with WooCommerce.

mainEntity.name: How do I get started with Tarasovs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fill out the contact form at tarasovs.me/contact-us or email work@tarasovs.me. We review the project, schedule a 30-minute discovery call, and send a detailed proposal within 48 hours — including scope, timeline, and investment.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer standalone SEO without a web design project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. SEO and GEO are available as standalone retainer services. One-time SEO audits are also available without an ongoing engagement.
